events.title: v0.1.0 The engine stands alone
events.detail: Split out of the code that rebuilt the DDWG introduction films: narration with a local speech model, soundtrack assembly, captions, picture staging and rendering, with a one-minute bilingual sample film.

events.title: v0.3.0 Concept contract and readings check
events.detail: A film declares what each concept means in its source and each edition's words for it; narration checks concepts and readings before any speech model loads.

events.title: v0.6.0 The picture gate
events.detail: check-picture runs the frame, sync and motion audits of the current composition and timeline and writes a gate record; without a passing record, nothing renders.

events.title: v0.8.0 Measured with the film's own fonts
events.detail: The headless audits measure text with the film's declared fonts; the gate record binds the stylesheet and each font by SHA-256.

events.title: v0.9.0 Named where it is spoken
events.detail: The gate refuses a mark that stands in speech for over 0.6 s before a name is legible, and speech of over 1 s with no legible name.

events.title: v0.10.0 The first production review
events.detail: The review command writes a film's first production review; before a render, preflight reports every stale or missing input at once.

events.title: v0.12.0 Every mark followed
events.detail: The motion audit follows each mark as a viewer sees it move and refuses halts, starts, races and pops; from this release it applies to every film.

events.title: v0.13.0 Uncaptioned pictures, four films
events.detail: Each edition renders a second picture without captions and proves it differs only by them; a delivery holds 25 members.

events.title: v0.14.0 Switches without a flash
events.detail: A version or captions switch in the player no longer shows the cover or a flat frame; the gate checks arcs that sweep a whole turn.

events.title: v0.17.0 Jumps and dash snaps
events.detail: The gate refuses marks that a stage cut moves whole, and strokes whose dashes snap within one frame.

events.title: v0.18.0 One author, no ringing
events.detail: The 1080p films average each 2×2 block between decode and encode, with a keyframe every 2 s; the verifier refuses films packaged earlier.

events.title: v0.19.0 Every frame compared
events.detail: compare-pictures compares every frame of an edition's two pictures and names each one-frame fault with the command that renders its picture again. Each film names its version, so a film packaged by an earlier release is refused.

events.title: v0.20.0 Drafts and repairs in the engine
events.detail: render-draft, fit and repair-pictures do in the engine what each film lane's scripts did, and a film may declare how its frames are captured; no film's bytes change.

events.title: v0.21.0 Still states refused, Spotlight read back
events.detail: check-picture refuses every still state that the reviewers count as off centre, and each piece a mark gains or loses whole within one frame. The sync audit judges each appearance of a label, and an English label by another form of its words. The verifier reads back the keywords and authors Spotlight imports from each film, and refuses films packaged earlier.

events.title: v0.21.1 Newer locks, the same takes
events.detail: The repository's tools move to ETHOS 0.2.0-beta.9, and the locks take newer releases, Pydantic 2.14.3 among them. Synthesized again under the new locks, the sample film's eight takes are byte-identical; mlx-audio stays 0.6.4.

events.title: v0.21.2 A Node security release
events.detail: The repository's Node moves to 26.13.1, a security release with nine fixes rated high. Node runs the picture pipeline, and the sample film builds and verifies on it.

events.title: v0.22.0 The sound judged before the picture
events.detail: check-sound judges an edition's assembled soundtrack before the picture follows it, by the review's own measures. A segment's voice clarity is measured as the reviewers measure it, and a caption cue holds its typeset text alone. compare-pictures measures the edge slivers of the two pictures at every frame.

events.title: v0.22.2 Endings judged where they are heard
events.detail: A stopped ending is judged where a listener hears the voice end, alike wherever its recording or soundtrack starts. A fall after which the sound rises again and dies away is a closure before its release, and the release is judged. Of 7,611 recorded takes, two change their verdict.

events.title: v0.22.3 Segments leveled within their chapter
events.detail: A script may declare segment_level_tolerance_db, from 0.1 to 3.0. The assembly then brings each segment farther than that from its chapter's median loudness to the edge of the tolerance, by one static gain of at most 2 dB, before it levels the chapters. A film that declares none assembles the same soundtrack and timeline as under 0.22.2.

events.title: v0.23.0 A fourth audit, pictures derived
events.detail: check-picture runs a fourth audit, the detail audit, and refuses a run far off centre; a film keeps such a finding by declaring an exception. A film that declares software capture derives its uncaptioned picture from the captioned one, and the 1080p films are encoded by x264. The declaration names the delivery folder as delivery_folder, and a delivery without --destination no longer goes to ~/Documents. preflight asks for the sound gate's record and the geometry record, and every production action and narration writes a duration record.

events.title: v0.23.1 Takes narrated anew
events.detail: The engine narrates with mlx-audio 0.6.6. A film that adopts the release narrates its takes anew, because the same seed gives another waveform; a film that keeps its takes holds mlx-audio at its present version in its own lock. The renderer moves to HyperFrames 0.9.64.

events.title: v0.24.0 Pictures drawn on a native canvas
events.detail: The engine draws a film's pictures on a native canvas of @napi-rs/canvas 1.1.1, with no browser: each frame is piped to x264, and a picture is drawn in four spans joined by stream copy. HyperFrames and GSAP are gone, and a film that adopts the release stages and renders its pictures again. One judgment of a take serves the audition, judge and converge, and converge settles an edition's narration without a targets file, a phrase or a seed from its author. A duration record states the host's load at its command's start and end.

events.title: v0.25.0 A review round prepared in one run
events.detail: review.round prepare writes a round's player binding and readback, measurements and prompts in one run; the commands prompts and bind are gone. filmkit.delivery.release writes a film's release manifest from its delivered build. python -m filmkit.adoption lists what a release asks of a film's tracked files, and an edition keeps no separate sync record.

events.title: v0.26.0 The packaged film's still scan
events.detail: produce scan-film scans each edition's packaged 1080p captioned film for still pictures under speech, and the delivery's verification and the delivery refuse an edition without its passing scan. converge asks whether a settled edition fits its runtime and exits 1 when it misses, and a build's sum counts the convergence. A cast may declare runtime_fit.reserve_seconds.

events.title: v0.27.0 The register check before narration
events.detail: python -m filmkit.register checks the words a viewer meets outside the picture against the formal register, with Vale 3.27.0, which the engine pins. Narration, preflight and review.round prepare refuse a film whose words hold an error-level form it has not excused; a film keeps a form at one place by [[register.exceptions]].

events.title: v0.28.0 A respelled name is a declared term
events.detail: A name that an edition respells in other letters must be a [[narration.terms]] term, and the readings check, judge, converge and audition refuse one that is not before any model loads. A take is held to its words, not to its respelling.

events.title: v0.29.0 An edition lasts as long as its narration
events.detail: The assembly counts each edition's runtime from its narration, rounded up to a whole second, and the declaration states credits_duration once; a script declares neither duration nor credits_duration. The two editions may differ in length, and converge no longer reports a missed runtime.

events.title: v0.30.0 Anchors in a script's own words
events.detail: A segment may mark anchors in its own words, and the timeline gives each its times, so a composition reads s.anchors[id] instead of searching for a phrase. Narration first draws each edition's picture over a timeline derived from its script, and refuses a script that does not mark an anchor its picture reads.

events.title: v0.31.0 Languages treated as equals
events.detail: One declaration for each language the engine builds holds that language's values, and a film's editions are its [editions.<code>] tables. Each edition's files stand at places its code derives, the pronunciation is split by edition, and what the engine derives is no longer declared.

events.title: v0.32.0 A record of every run
events.detail: Every command of an edition's build chain writes a run record of each input and output by its SHA-256. filmkit plan states each node's state, and filmkit verify hashes every recorded file; a review round's preparation and a release's record run it first.

events.title: v0.33.0 English heard by its pronunciation
events.detail: In an English edition a transcript's word passes the units line where its pronunciation in the pinned CMUdict, which the supply places, is one of the text word's readings. The author's hearing of a take settles the lines it names for that take, and a take under its clarity line waits for the author's ear.

events.title: v0.34.0 A film built by its verbs
events.detail: One console command, filmkit, builds a film by its verbs, among them check, narrate, build, verify, deliver and release. The production command, the pre-render check, the duration records, the adoption command and the media server are removed. Every node but the source check and the two gates binds only the declaration's tables its run reads.

events.title: v0.35.0 Balance measured on the content
events.detail: check-picture refuses a run of 1.5 s or more through which the mass of the scene drawn stands more than 90 px off x 960, and each still state of 2 s or more that stands more than 50 px off y 510. A new mass audit draws the uncaptioned stage as the renderer does and encodes nothing.
